dek: The third version of jodriscoll.com: an Astro 7 site on Cloudflare Workers, written for two readers at once, the person deciding whether to hire me and the AI agent screening the application first.
short: The third and current version of my portfolio: an Astro 7 site on Cloudflare Workers. 94 pages render at build time and ship as static assets; a Worker answers the contact form and a JSON content API.

items.name: Cloudflare Workers
items.note: static assets plus a Worker for /api

delivery.summary: The site builds and deploys from my machine with Wrangler. Pushing to GitHub doesn't deploy; a release is a build and one deploy command.

steps.name: Build
steps.detail: astro build renders 94 routes to static HTML: every page, project, post, the feeds and the machine-readable files.

steps.name: Assets
steps.detail: The rendered pages, styles, fonts and screenshots upload to Workers static assets. Unchanged files are skipped.

steps.name: Worker
steps.detail: The /api routes (contact form, events and the content API) run on the Worker with nodejs_compat.

steps.name: Secrets
steps.detail: The Resend keys are Worker secrets, set with wrangler secret bulk. They never enter the repository.

steps.name: Domain
steps.detail: jodriscoll.com is a custom domain on the Worker. DNS stays on the Cloudflare zone it has used for years.

highlights.title: Written for the screener too
highlights.text: Applications are often read by an AI agent before a person. Every project, role and post is also published as JSON-LD, llms.txt, JSON Resume and a JSON content API, from the same content files the pages use.

highlights.title: One source of truth
highlights.text: Projects are one JSON spec each. The Work page, project pages, resume, feeds and API all read from them, so a fact changes in one place.

highlights.title: Static first
highlights.text: Every page is rendered at build time. The Worker only runs for the contact form and the API, so pages load as plain files from Cloudflare's network.

highlights.title: From Pages to Workers
highlights.text: Ver. 2 built on Cloudflare Pages from Git. Ver. 3 moved to Workers with static assets, which the Astro adapter now targets, and kept the domain, DNS and account where they were.

highlights.title: No client framework
highlights.text: Interactions (filters, the timeline, the contents bar, the contact sheet) are small inline scripts on top of HTML and CSS.
